task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after form-submit gating, action routing, local-event dispatch, asynchronous scheduling, form-input collection, tuple normalization and projection preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable query_payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the console sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name query_payload is assembled from string fragments at the sink, so a direct literal search does not reveal the anchor.
Form input values are normalized, projected and transported through dynamic lanes before the payload is emitted.

The form-submit path crosses filter arming, enabled gating, action routing, local event dispatch, route layers, asynchronous scheduling, tuple construction, runtime slot materialization, payload construction, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
Decoy modules call the alternate reducer selector y() to emit qp-like shadow values that do not feed the requested query_payload field.
The target value is separated from the form submit by DOM CustomEvent, Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The final sink receives an already-constructed query_payload value after projection and transport recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is a deterministic transform of form input fields (scope, filter mode, sort key, page, limit) and the active reducer recipe, emitted to the console under action request.transform. It is not a browser fingerprint, state encoding, byte-array transform or request signature.

near_categories.why_not: The value is derived from multiple form fields through a reducer recipe rather than encoding a single state token.
The output has no cryptographic proof/seal semantics; it is a transform of request inputs, not a signature over them.
